title: Agile Specialist - Allergan Aesthetics
description:
About AbbVie
At Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, we develop, manufacture, and market a portfolio of leading aesthetics brands and products. Our aesthetics portfolio includes facial injectables, body contouring, plastics, skin care, and more. Our goal is to consistently provide our customers with innovation, education, exceptional service, and a commitment to excellence, all with a personal touch. For more information, visit https://global.allerganaesthetics.com/ . Follow Allergan Aesthetics on LinkedIn.
As the Agile Specialist, you will report to the Senior Manager, Agile Practices as well as
continuously collaborate with key stakeholders across the business to solve the most important
technical problems.
You Will:
• Lead and refine continuous planning, ensuring ongoing planning for and visibility to a
rolling quarter + plan for the team/s you support.
• Maintain engineering team schedules, ensuring proper resource planning and translation
of estimates to key milestone dates.
• Track project milestones, dependencies, deliverables, and timelines to ensure projects
and programs stay on track and meet delivery timelines.
• Remove obstacles that may hinder the team's progress.
• Coordinate communication between different teams, departments, and stakeholders.
• Collaborate with Engineering, Product, and PMO to manage and prioritize the product
backlog.
• Ensure engineers have necessary product requirements and UX designs to stay on track
and meet deadlines.
• Serve as the key liaison between software development teams and external
stakeholders building advocacy and credibility.
• Facilitate Agile ceremonies such as daily stand-ups, sprint planning, backlog
maintenance and refinement, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.
• Promote Agile best practices and educate team members to enhance team performance
and productivity.
• Support the JIRA management for teams they support and other tools as appropriate.
• Provide burndown charts, velocity tracking, and other agile performance metrics to
inform and resolve issues with the team and manager(s).
Required Experience & Skills:
• Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Technology, or related field.
• 5+ years’ experience in an Agile environment with experience using Agile methodologies
such as Scrum or Kanban.
• Excellent organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.
• Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams.
• Strong problem-solving skills and adaptability.
• Proficiency in JIRA, Confluence, and related tooling.

title: Associate Director, Business Insights Lead
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Purpose
Reporting to the Director, Strategy, Analytics & Business Insights (SABI), the Associate Director, Business Insights serves as the primary analytical and strategic partner to the Clinical Site Management (CSM) organization. This role owns portfolio-level business insights for Clinical Site Management — translating complex, ambiguous business questions into data-driven analyses that directly inform Sr. Director and VP-level decisions across site strategy, study design, resourcing, and risk management. The Associate Director builds and sustains trusted relationships with Sr. Directors and their leadership teams across all geographic areas and across the clinical study lifecycle, ensuring SABI’s analytical capabilities are embedded into how every leader plans and executes their operation strategies.
Responsibilities
Strategic Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement: Serve as the primary SABI point of contact and trusted advisor to Area heads and Clinical Field Excellence leadership, proactively identifying where data and analytics can resolve ambiguity in portfolio-level decisions.
End-to-End Insight Delivery: Lead delivery of portfolio-level insights — from hypothesis generation and data identification through analysis, insight generation, and recommendations — following SABI’s hypothesis-driven problem-solving approach.
Analytical Product Ownership: Own and evolve key analytical products for Clinical Site Management (e.g., site ID and allocation models, country/site performance benchmarking, enrollment scenario planning, operational trend analyses), ensuring they remain decision-relevant as portfolio priorities shift.
Cross-Geographic Support — Americas to Europe to Intercontinental: Provide analytical and decision-support coverage to all global stakeholders, extending proven approaches where transferable and adapting them to country/region-specific needs.
Business Need Translation: Partner with Sr. Directors and CSM leadership across all functions to translate emerging business needs into scoped, actionable analytical workstreams.
Executive Communication: Influence Sr. Directors/VP-level decisions, tailoring communication to executive audiences.
Risk & Gap Identification: Identify and escalate structural gaps or unaddressed risks within the CSM functions that are not yet visible to leadership, bringing an independent analytical lens to surface them.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate with SABI’s other leads (across CSL and CSM) and adjacent CAP functions (Study Feasibility & Analytics, Clinical Acceleration Solutions) to ensure consistency and reuse of analytical approaches across therapeutic areas.
CDO-Wide Initiatives: Provide analytical and strategic support for priority CDO-wide initiatives, partnering across functions and applying SABI capabilities beyond assigned therapeutic areas to advance enterprise objectives.
Team Capability Development: Provide project-based coaching and mentorship to junior team members and rotational analysts supporting SABI work, while maintaining accountability for the quality and analytical rigor of assigned outputs.
Global Stewardship: Maintain a global mindset with an objective and long-term view of stakeholder needs across all CSM functions, balancing responsiveness to Sr. Director requests with SABI’s focus on high-impact, analytically complex work.
Required:
Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree in Finance, Analytics, Business, or related quantitative field preferred
10+ years of relevant experience in business analytics, strategy, or a related client-facing analytical role, ideally within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or healthcare. 5+ years of relevant experience for advanced degree holders (e.g. PhD, MD, PharmD)
Demonstrated experience managing senior stakeholder relationships (Director/Sr. Director level or above), including delivering findings and recommendations to executive audiences
Strong analytical and strategic decision-support skills, with the ability to translate ambiguous business questions into structured, data-driven analyses
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to distill complex analyses into clear, actionable insights for non-technical audiences
Experience with data analytics/visualization tools (e.g., SQL, Power BI, Excel)
Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams independently, across more than one therapeutic area or stakeholder group, with sound judgment on prioritization and escalation
Familiarity with clinical trial operations, drug development, or R&D processes
Experience supporting multiple therapeutic areas or portfolios concurrently
Preferred:
Prior people-management or mentoring experience
Working knowledge of AbbVie systems and organizational structure

title: Associate Director, Global Business Development Forecasting
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Business Development is a critical pillar of AbbVie’s future growth, and Global Business Development Forecasting helps determine which external opportunities can create the greatest long-term value. The team brings commercial insight, analytical rigor, and strategic clarity to high-stakes BD decisions by translating science, market dynamics, competitive context, and uncertainty into actionable forecasts.
The Associate Director plays a high-impact and highly visible role in this process, leading forecasts and commercial perspectives that shape executive understanding of opportunity value, risk, and strategic fit. Working across R&D, Commercial, Pipeline Commercial Strategy, CBSO, BD Finance, and other partners, this role sits at the intersection of scientific innovation and commercial strategy and directly supports decisions that influence AbbVie’s future portfolio.
Success requires strong forecasting and commercial analytics expertise, rigorous assumption development, clear executive communication, and the ability to influence across a matrixed organization. Candidates should be curious, collaborative, comfortable with ambiguity, and able to create structure in fast-moving situations. For the right candidate, the role offers meaningful growth through exposure to senior leaders, enterprise-wide relationships, and deeper understanding of both R&D and Commercial strategy.
This role reports to the Director, Global Business Development Forecasting.
Responsibilities
Lead commercial forecasting, market assessments, scenario analyses, and commercial P&Ls for BD opportunities, balancing analytical rigor with timely decision support in a fast-paced environment.
Develop patient-based forecast models, pressure-test assumptions, and apply primary research, secondary data, epidemiology, competitive intelligence, market access input, and expert perspectives to build a well-supported commercial view.
Partner broadly across BD, PCS, finance, market access, epidemiology, marketing analytics, and senior leadership to align assumptions, clarify risks and opportunities, and ensure commercial perspectives are reflected in deal valuation and governance discussions.
Translate complex analyses into clear recommendations, executive-ready narratives, and decision options for senior leaders and governance forums, facilitating productive discussion around uncertainty, trade-offs, and strategic implications.
Advance BD forecasting capabilities by sharing best practices, improving tools and processes, and helping create faster, more consistent, and audit-ready ways of working.
Education and experience:  7+ years of relevant forecasting, market analytics, finance, or life sciences consulting experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, or related industries; MBA or other advanced degree preferred. Bachelor’s degree in finance/accounting or business required.
Forecasting and analytics skills:  Experience building forecast models in Excel and forecasting platforms such as IQVIA Forecast Horizon; ability to develop and/or utilize patient-flow modeling approaches, craft robust assumptions, and prepare evidence-based forecast inputs from epidemiology, secondary data, market research, treatment dynamics, competitive profiles, and expert input.  Familiar with key data sources used to substantiate forecast recommendations and demonstrated ability to clearly document forecast assumption logic and rationale.  Familiarity with using and crafting Target Product Profiles (TPPs), establishing and aligning analytical business rules and market definitions, and leveraging claims data analytics is also highly desirable.
Business and therapeutic area knowledge:  Experience supporting strategic decision making in specialized therapeutic areas such as Neuroscience, Immunology, Oncology, or other complex markets is preferred; ability to apply data, assumptions, and market context effectively is critical.
Communication and influence:  Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to tailor messages by audience, translate complex quantitative analyses into recommendations and decision options, and influence stakeholders across functions and cultures without direct authority.
Project leadership:  Strong project management skills in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment, with the ability to prioritize multiple workstreams, communicate trade-offs, escalate risks appropriately, and deliver high-quality work under time pressure.

The Analytics & Performance Excellence (APEX) function supports AbbVie’s US organization and is comprised of highly respected researchers, analysts, data scientists and strategists who are committed to being best-in-class within the biopharmaceutical industry.  We serve as a strategic in-house counsel, ensuring that all decisions leverage the key insights that we develop.  We continue to build new capabilities and skill sets, encouraging our team members to pull up a chair, be themselves, be creative, speak their minds, and do good work.  We are a passionate, diverse, flexible, and inclusive organization with a culture that supports the best ideas, wherever they originate.
The Market Access & Patient Services (MAPS) organization within the Analytics & Performance Excellence (APEX) team plays an instrumental role in shaping market access and patient service strategies for all of AbbVie’s domestic brands. As a member of this team, you will plan and execute standard and ad-hoc analytics to identify/ quantify payer opportunities and threats, make specific recommendations on the development of market access/patient service strategies and tactics, develop analytical capabilities, enable organizational learning, and ensure alignment of analytical insights with the broader commercial goals of each brand. The role requires foundational data analytics training and experience in the pharmaceutical or related industry. The role provides insights that directly impact patient and physician access to AbbVie brands through its influence on the development of pricing, contracting and other strategies.
MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES
Execute standard/ ad-hoc analytics on a key brand focused on providing insights that influence market access strategy through data analytics, customer insights and business knowledge. Assist in the development with U.S. Market Access commercial leaders, innovative Pricing and Contracting strategies to achieve optimal payer formulary access that maximize net sales for assigned Specialty therapeutic areas. Identify through claims analysis, market dynamics that shape brand demand and build models to portray risks, opportunities, and sensitivities. Demonstrate foundational understanding of the U.S. healthcare landscape and key AbbVie therapeutic areas to identify and proactively address opportunities and threats. Build collaborative relationships with internal U.S. Market Access Sales and Marketing stakeholders. Align insights to Brand insight partners, that when integrated with HCP and Consumer insights, positively impacts brand decision making.
Key areas of functional scope include:
Delivering analytics to inform GPO, Specialty Pharmacy, Health Plan and PBM contracting strategies for specialty brands across payer channels through data modelling techniques, conveying analytical narratives that describe the opportunity and risks of stakeholder negotiations, and informing financial projections based on launch pricing and contracting strategies.
Delivering brand specific market access analytical insights in response to specific market access issues/ trends. Understanding the impact of utilization management, tiering and medical policy impact on overall demand, line of therapy and co-pay support. Conducting investigative analytics to validate and/ or quantify market phenomenon related to competitive or customer tactics. Identifying through quantitative methods, value drivers that guide clinical data development and value positioning.
Demonstrating a foundational understanding of syndicated and AbbVie proprietary data, data science and modeling techniques and the ability to synthesize insights into compelling narratives. Under guidance, is proficient at supplier and stakeholder management, executing external analytics to deliver compelling learnings, and executing analytical strategies appropriate for the issue at hand.
Responsible for effective communication of market access analytical insights to leadership.

Bachelor’s degree
2 - 4 years of professional experience.
2+ years of related industry experience in data analytics.
Proficient in SQL, Python, or other experience in querying structured databases for insights.
Strong story telling skills; ability to distill complex information synthesized into concise and impactful messages and communications.

Ability to provide direction for functional area.

Purpose:
AbbVie is seeking a highly motivated, scientifically rigorous and collaborative postdoctoral fellow to join the Materials Science & Characterization Team in PDST / PPG Analytical to advance AI-enabled, multimodal characterization of targeted lipid nanoparticles (tLNPs). This position offers an opportunity to lead the generation, integration, and curation of an analytical dataset using experimental characterization data generated internally and data received predominantly from external laboratories and contract research organizations (CROs). During the first half of the appointment, the primary focus will be on analytical data generation, data quality assessment, standardization, and curation; during the second half, the fellow will increasingly apply feature extraction and interpretable statistical and machine-learning analyses to identify attributes associated with particle heterogeneity, stability, product quality, and functional performance in support of tLNP development.  The successful candidate will design and execute experiments, analyze and interpret data, collaborate with multidisciplinary partners, and contribute to scientific publications, presentations, and internal knowledge sharing. The goal of this position is to generate new insights, methods, or capabilities that advance Product Development Science & Technology priorities and support innovation of future commercial delivery approaches for Oncology and Immunology Therapies.

Own and execute fit-for-purpose tLNP analytical-data programs, incorporating internally generated data and analytical data received predominantly from external laboratories and CROs, in alignment with project objectives.
Design rigorous experiments and analytical workflows ; define data-transfer, quality-assessment, and documentation requirements for internally and externally generated datasets; and establish consistent reporting standards to support high-quality tLNP development and decision-making.
Define and manage batch metadata, sampling strategies, sample-tracking requirements, and provenance for samples and data generated internally or received from external partners
Build, integrate curate, and maintain validated multimodal characterization datasets across analytical platforms, with an initial emphasis on data generation, quality assessment, harmonization, and curation.
Analyze and harmonize quantitative features related to particle size, morphology, aggregation, thermal behavior, spectroscopy, encapsulation, and accessibility.
Following establishment of a sufficiently curated analytical dataset, develop and apply interpretable statistical, computational, and machine-learning approaches to identify quality-relevant attributes, fingerprint batches, assess heterogeneity and stability risks, and evaluate structure–function relationships.

Strong combination of hands-on experimental expertise, analytical data generation and curation experience, quantitative data analysis, multivariate statistics, and an interest in developing interpretable machine-learning approaches.

title: Senior Manager, Community Policy
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
In Community Policy, our mission is to create and evolve principled policies that establish the rules of the road for guests and hosts across Airbnb. This involves solving some of the most complex Trust & Safety challenges of our time. Our work is informed by rigorous research and stakeholder collaboration, and we design policies that can support our community at scale. We team with our cross-functional partners to create accessible policy enforcement guides and to continuously maintain and improve our policies.
The Difference You Will Make:
As a Senior Manager for Community Policy, you will partner closely with stakeholders across the company to support Airbnb's strategic objectives. You will lead policy development in the anti-discrimination and safety space, addressing real-world harms and ensuring every host and guest is treated fairly. This role entails understanding the needs of hosts and guests and collaborating closely with our operations, legal, business, design, and product teams. The policies you build will directly shape how millions of hosts and guests experience Airbnb and their confidence in the platform.
About You
You are a seasoned policy leader who loves solving complex problems and collaborating cross-functionally.
You have deep expertise in the anti-discrimination space and a track record in safety policies addressing real-world harms.
You are an excellent communicator with exceptional writing skills.
You are an adept presenter with experience engaging with all levels of leadership, including senior executives.
You are a team player who thrives in a fast-moving environment and brings a strategic mindset and bias toward execution.
You are principled, have meticulous attention to detail, and incorporate diverse perspectives in pursuit of the best decisions and outcomes possible.
You are experienced at developing and implementing policies and measuring their effectiveness.
You are proactively data-driven: you don't wait for problems to surface — you seek out data, research, and insights to identify gaps and opportunities to improve policies before they become issues.
A Typical Day:
Have broad ownership over our policies affecting trust in Airbnb, especially in the anti-discrimination and safety space
Lead policy development and draft clear and scalable policy frameworks that keep pace with company priorities
Foster, build, and maintain relationships with cross-functional stakeholders across the business including Operations, Legal, Anti-Discrimination and Equity, Public Policy, Product, Communications, and Supply, acting as a trusted policy partner who helps teams move forward
Guide policy operationalization efforts in partnership with cross-functional stakeholders
Proactively use data, research, and community insights to evaluate existing policies, identify improvement opportunities, and drive revisions before issues escalate
Serve as subject matter expert to provide sound policy guidance for time-sensitive escalations, including from Operations and company leadership
Your Expertise:
10-15+ years of experience in a Policy, Legal, or Trust and Safety role
Prior policy leadership addressing discrimination and safety issues in a complex international setting
Thoughtful business judgment, strategic thinking, and ability to work well under pressure
Exceptional writing and communication skills
Demonstrated capacity for critical thinking, research, and analysis
Strong attention to detail
A track record of strong leadership and an ability to independently manage a portfolio of challenging issues
Fluency in data analysis and leading data-driven decision-making
Deep understanding of the end-to-end policy process and how to influence policy delivery
Experience working in a matrix and driving solutions to complex problems through cross-functional collaboration
Ability to explain and simplify complex information to others

This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with us if the state you live in is on the exclusion list  If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from.

description:
Do you love creating elegant solutions to highly complex challenges? Do you intrinsically see the importance in every detail? Custom Circuit design methodology
Leading/managing projects
Knowledge of Cache design/architecture, memory hierarchy and scripting is a huge plus

title: Design Verification Engineer
description:
At Apple, we work every single day to craft products that enrich people’s lives. Do you love working on challenges that no one has solved yet and changing the game? We have an opportunity for an outstandingly hardworking design verification engineer! As a member of our wide-ranging group, you will have the rare and extraordinary opportunity to craft upcoming products that will delight and encourage millions of Apple’s customers daily.
This role is for a DV engineer who will enable us to produce fully functional first silicon for IP designs. The responsibilities include all phases of pre-silicon verification including but not limited to: establishing DV methodology, test-plan development, verification environment development including stimulus and checkers, test-writing, debug, coverage, sign-off for RTL freeze and tape-out.
In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring bug-free first silicon for part of the SoC / IP and are encouraged to develop detailed test and coverage plans based on the micro-architecture. You are responsible for developing verification methodology suitable for the IP, ensuring a scalable and portable environment. You will get to develop verification environment, including all the respective components such as stimulus, checkers, assertions, trackers, coverage. A mindset to break the design is highly desirable.
Furthermore, you will develop verification plans for all features under your care, execute verification plans, including design bring-up, DV environment bring- up, regression enabling features, and debug of the test failures. You will also learn to develop block, IP and SoC level test-benches track and report DV progress using a variety of metrics, including bugs and coverage. You will also be expected to make use of LLM and related technologies to achieve efficient execution and improved quality.
Minimum qualifications: BS degree in technical subject area and a minimum 3 years relevant industry experience or equivalent.
Preferred qualifications: MS degree in a technical subject area and relevant industry experience strongly preferred
Strong knowledge of OOP, SystemVerilog and UVM
Strong knowledge in developing scalable and portable testbenches
Proven experience with verification methodologies and tools such as simulators, waveform viewer, build and run automation, coverage collection, and gate-level simulations
Working experience using LLMs for efficiency and quality
Experience with power-aware (UPF) or similar verification methodology
Knowledge of one of the scripting languages such as Python, Perl, TCL
Some experience with serial protocols such as PCIe or USB, parallel protocol such as DDR is a plus but not required
Knowledge of formal verification methodology is a plus but not required

title: Digital Mixed Signal Design and Modeling Engineer
description:
Join our team at Apple developing complex mixed-signal IPs for Apple’s custom integrated circuits. Our team has shipped hundreds of millions of chips into Apple’s existing product lines, and is developing new chips for future product lines!
In this role, you will create high-speed behavioral models for complex analog IPs that interface with digital control logic. Your models will “close the loop” in mixed-signal simulations, catch cross-domain bugs, and deliver 10x to 1000x speedups over transistor-level simulations—driving critical productivity gains across Apple's next-generation silicon roadmap. We are a prolific, diverse team looking for an enthusiastic engineer ready to build industry-leading products that surprise and delight our customers.
• Collaborate with system architects, analog designers, and digital teams to establish precise model specifications for mixed-signal IPs.
• Develop high-speed models from schematics and design specs.
• Build mixed-signal testbenches and integrate models into projects to close the simulation loop.
• Develop verification plans, run regression suites, and debug digital/analog corner cases.
• Correlate model accuracy and performance against transistor-level SPICE simulations.
• Drive modeling methodologies to accelerate simulation turnaround times and ensure tapeout readiness.
Minimum qualifications: BS and a minimum of 3 years of relevant industry experience
Preferred qualifications: Master's Degree in relevant field of study preferred
Experience developing digital logic or behavioral models for analog and mixed-signal circuits (e.g., SystemVerilog, Real Number Modeling / RNM, or Verilog-A/AMS).
Solid fundamentals in digital design and RTL development (SystemVerilog/Verilog).
Good knowledge of analog circuits and architectures (e.g., power converters, regulators, references, ADCs/DACs).
Experience with industry-standard simulation and verification tools (e.g., Xcelium, Virtuoso).
Strong debugging and cross-functional communication skills.

description:
Join Apple's Human Interface Design (HID) team to develop advanced sensing, tracking, and classification algorithms to enable best-in-class user experiences across Mac, iPhone, iPad, Apple Pencil, Apple Watch, and exciting new products. We are looking for a strong machine learning & DSP engineer with a passion for bridging algorithm development with embedded system design and software integration and leveraging GenAI tools into an engineering workflow. Our team brings togethers experts of diverse backgrounds: Machine Learning, Signal Processing, Firmware, Software, Physics, Mathematics, Human Factors, and more. You will work at the intersection of hardware, software, and design, collaborating with specialists across Apple to ship extraordinary products used every day by millions of people around the world.
This is an machine learning engineering role at the HW/SW/UI boundary, with broad collaboration opportunities across firmware, software, and algorithms teams. You will be responsible for developing sensing algorithms using signal processing and machine learning techniques and delivering them as highly optimized, power-efficient code for custom silicon. You'll tackle complex challenges like memory constraints, computational budgets, and real-time performance while ensuring robust end-to-end functionality from sensor data acquisition through to the software layer to deliver exceptional user experiences. In this role, you will also lead efforts to identify, evaluate, and deploy GenAI tools that improve team productivity, including GenAI-assisted development, data analysis, and workflow automation. description:

description:

title: SoC Power Spec Engineer
description:
Do you have a passion for crafting new solutions? As part of our Silicon Engineering group, you will generate ideas and turn them into reality. You will be part of the team responsible for crafting state-of-the-art ASICs that are integral to many Apple products. We are looking for an engineer who will work on the modeling of power dissipation of various IPs and applications, including AI/ML and power modeling at the SOC/system level for Apple products. This role provides an opportunity to participate in optimization of a variety of leading edge chips for power-efficiency. You will collaborate across many teams including architecture, SOC design, and system design. The job also involves partnering with the lab and silicon characterization/validation teams on correlating the models to the silicon data.
The job involves collaborating across many fields and playing a role of getting innovative products to millions of customers. You will have the opportunity to build new insights into silicon optimization, as well as work with architects, silicon design engineers, software developers, and be involved in silicon/model correlation efforts of mobile SoC design.
Your main responsibilities will be:
-Modeling power dissipation at the SOC level, including Neural Engines, CPUs, Graphics, compute ( AI/ML) accelerators, media IPs, caches and fabric.
-Modeling power dissipation for customer use-cases.
-Interacting with the System designers, Technology team, Silicon Validation, and Product Engineering teams to define power targets at the SOC level, and the power delivery.
-Working with the power lab and test teams to correlate models to silicon data.
Minimum qualifications: A minimum of a bachelor's degree in relevant field and a minimum of 10 years of relevant industry experience.
Preferred qualifications: We would prefer our SoC Power Spec Engineer to have the following qualifications:
MSEE preferred
Deep knowledge of SOC architecture and power modeling.
Deep understanding of SOC building blocks including CPU, GPU, caches, memory and media IPs
Skills in scripting and data analysis.
Understanding of VLSI design flow and CMOS technology and background in EE.
Ability to understand and model thermal control loops and throttling mechanisms.
Strong teammate with excellent communication skills.

description:

- Improve power measurement infrastructure.

description:
Apple services depend upon performant and reliable networking primitives. Our mission is to connect all services in secure, scalable and transparent matter. 5+ years of relevant industry experience
Professional expertise in software engineering

Full product lifecycle ownership mindset (design → implementation → production)
Experience with core production engineering best practices (e.g., designing for operability and scalability, adopting SLOs, eliminating toil).

title: Embedded Software Engineer, Microcontrollers
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Embedded Software Engineer on the Embedded MCU team, you'll own the microcontroller firmware that directly controls Base's power hardware: the batteries, inverters, and disconnect systems in every home we serve. You'll write the bare-metal and RTOS software from control logic, state machines, and fault handling down through drivers, BSP/HAL, and peripheral configuration, and it has to run flawlessly and safely in the field.

 

As Base's hardware portfolio grows, you'll lead the bring-up of new boards, build reusable firmware libraries that make each new product faster to ship, and act as the primary software partner to our hardware and power electronics engineers on the HW/SW boundary. You'll design deterministic real-time control and protection within hard timing budgets, own device communications over CAN, and see your firmware deployed across a rapidly growing fleet.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the business logic running on Base's microcontrollers: state machines, control and sequencing logic, fault handling, and safety coordination for our batteries, inverters, and disconnect systems.

 - Lead new hardware bring-up end to end, from peripheral configuration and driver development through BSP/HAL integration, and cut the time it takes to get new boards running.

 - Implement and tune deterministic real-time control and protection on multi-core MCUs, partitioning work across cores and staying within hard ISR timing and jitter budgets.

 - Build and maintain the device communications stack, including CAN/CAN-FD drivers, buffering, and transport reliability, plus higher-level protocols and the firmware-update flows that run over them.

 - Serve as the primary software interface to Hardware Engineering: join schematic reviews, weigh in on processor and peripheral selection, pin assignments, and timing, and debug HW/SW integration issues on the bench.

 - Build reusable firmware libraries and coding standards in place of product-specific implementations, so each new product ships faster than the last.

 - Take new products from prototype through production firmware and into the field, using hardware-in-the-loop testing and crash dumps to drive down field-reported firmware issues.

 


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Hands-on experience shipping bare-metal and/or RTOS firmware on modern microcontrollers (e.g. ARM Cortex-M), including taking one or more products to manufacturing.

Build and scale Apollo router infrastructure , supporting multi-region deployments, routing, and failover.
Implement CI/CD pipelines and governance workflows to ensure safe schema evolution and avoid breaking API changes.
Develop capabilities for multi-tenant routing and Apollo contracts to support external and internal product use cases.

We're looking for someone to help scale DoorDash's next billion dollar business, DashMart, by growing our in-house food program, DashMart Kitchens. The DashMart Kitchens team is focused on building a new type of restaurant platform within DashMart, offering a broad selection of prepared foods and well-known restaurant staples to our customers' doorsteps.
About the Role
As the Kitchen Manager for DashMart Kitchens (DMK), you’ll lead the daily operations of a DoorDash-owned kitchen located within a DashMart fulfillment center. You’ll oversee a team of operations associates and shift leads to ensure every meal is prepared safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards.
You’ll combine hands-on culinary leadership with operational excellence — managing staffing, scheduling, and kitchen performance while ensuring food safety, order accuracy, and team success. You’ll work closely with your Site Manager to lead multiple food concepts, improve processes, and create a great place to work. This role requires strict adherence to food safety, inventory controls, and safety protocols due to routine access to food, supplies, equipment, and operational systems.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you...
Thrive on iteration and have experience leading teams through changes
Are excited about coaching, managing, and leading teams in fast-paced environments
Enjoy building systems and processes and seeing ideas come to life
Are eager to learn how different parts of a complex operation connect
Are obsessed with preparing consistent, high-quality food for customers
Want to grow in delivery-only kitchen operations
You’ll Make an Impact By...
Leading: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Kitchen Operations Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. Because this position supervises staff and is responsible for maintaining a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace, strong adherence to professional conduct, clear communication, and employee safety standards is required. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your DMK, helping your team to navigate new food concepts and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners.
Operating and Building Systems: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results for your kitchen. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success by building, implementing, and improving systems for effective scheduling, ensuring par levels are met, executing recipes accurately, and deploying best practices.Because this role oversees high-risk kitchen equipment and fast-paced food production, maintaining sound judgment and unimpaired performance is essential to ensure a safe work environment. You’ll engage cross-functional partners within DoorDash as needed for support.
Strategizing: You will analyze performance metrics, identify root causes of issues like prep gaps or order quality, and implement solutions that drive efficiency and adoption. You will refine processes, and partner with your Site Manager and cross-functional teams to execute new initiatives and continuously improve how the kitchen operates.
Delighting: You care deeply about delivering great food and a great customer experience. You will coach your team to maintain recipe accuracy, food safety, and storefront availability, knowing that consistency is key in a multi-concept kitchen. You will collaborate with central teams so your site has the tools, training, and support needed to achieve excellent quality outcomes.
We’re excited about you because…
You have 3+ years of experience in a medium/high-volume fast-casual or full-service restaurant environment.
You have 2+ years of experience leading teams, including hiring, scheduling, coaching, and performance management.
You hold (or are willing to get) a ServeSafe Manager certification and set high standards for food safety and cleanliness.
You’re a hands-on leader who motivates teams of 5+ employees to perform and grow.
You take ownership and thrive in fast-changing, startup-style environments where no task is too big or small.
You’re a creative problem solver who challenges “how it’s always been done” and finds better ways forward.
You’re analytical, data-driven, and comfortable using Excel or Google Sheets to make decisions.
As the leader of the site, you will need to ensure your team and the site is fully supported, which will include regularly scheduled late-night and weekend hours.
You’re comfortable flexing between kitchen and fulfillment operations, and you understand how culinary execution and order flow connect to overall site metrics like accuracy, quality, and efficiency.
You have (or can quickly learn) a working knowledge of inventory management systems (IMS), product flow, and fulfillment best practices within a multi-operation site.

 - Experience planning and coordinating maintenance activities, including shutdowns, repairs, and continuous improvement projects.

 - Flexibility to support off-shift, weekend, or emergency maintenance activities as business needs require.

 - Experience using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) such as MaintainX, SAP, Maximo, or similar.

 - Proficiency with Microsoft Office and maintenance reporting tools.

 - Experience using Building Automation System software to monitor all factory systems connected, diagnose & correct faults with facility equipment.

 - Experience troubleshooting Factory Utility Systems. Examples include: Process Cooling Towers, Boilers, Chillers, Air Compressors, Fire Alarm Systems, Fire Suppression Systems, Electrical Power Emergency Generators, Battery Backup Centers, Security Camera Networks, Badge Door Access with Card Readers & Turnstiles systems.

 - Strong electrical, HVAC, controls, automation, mechanical, and pneumatic troubleshooting skills.

title: Lead Inspector & Stacker
description:
YOUR ROLE
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Lead and support production team members to meet daily manufacturing targets.
Communicate shift goals, updates, and expectations clearly to team members.
Serve as a role model for attendance, performance, and workplace behavior.
Support shift handoffs by communicating key updates and issues to maintenance or supervisors.
Inspect boards and ensure visual and dimensional quality standards are met.
Use QA inspection tools to measure the quality of products.
Follow QA standards to ensure we are producing a quality product.
Provide proper training for all new end of line associates.
Monitor and provide coaching and feedback regarding work performance of end of line associates.
Communicate with extruder operators to ensure a quality end product.
Review work order and ensure correct tags and color.
Manage line documentation.
Ensure packaging specification are met.
Ensure clean and organized work areas are maintained in accordance with 6S and housekeeping standards.
Adheres to Fiberon’s safety requirements.
Assist with managing the production floor (breaks, absences, etc.)
WORK ENVIRONMENT
Manufacturing environment with exposure to: Heat, noise, dust, and moving machinery
May require availability outside of standard hours to support troubleshooting or continuous operations.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
Strength & Endurance Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull objects weighing between 20 to 50 pounds independently (over 50 pounds with buddy lift), including cleaning equipment, dust collection systems, and raw materials.
Perform repetitive tasks such as sweeping, brushing, vacuuming, and operating tools like staple guns and banders.
Stand and walk for extended periods (8 to 12-hour shifts) during production and cleaning tasks.
Maintain stamina and focus to perform physically demanding tasks without fatigue.
Mobility & Flexibility Bend, squat, stoop, kneel, crawl, and stretch to reach and clean various areas, inspect equipment, and align materials.
Climb ladders and work at heights to access dust accumulation and perform maintenance tasks.
Reach or work above shoulder level as needed.
Dexterity & Coordination Use hand tools such as brushes, brooms, scrapers, and vacuums with precision and good hand-eye coordination.
Handle packaging materials, attach labels, and refill equipment accurately and efficiently.
Visual & Sensory Acuity Good vision required to identify dust accumulation, inspect product quality, and monitor screens and labels.
Ability to perform color and defect inspections with close attention to detail.
Maintain balance and spatial awareness to ensure safety and stability in a dynamic environment.
Environmental Tolerance Work in hot, noisy, dusty, and/or humid conditions for extended periods.
Tolerate exposure to moving mechanical parts, vibrations, and varying temperatures.
Wear personal protective equipment (PPE) such as masks, respirators, safety glasses, earplugs, and gloves for long durations.
Communication & Safety Communicate effectively with team members regarding defects, operational issues, and safety concerns.
Recognize personal physical limits and request assistance when tasks become too demanding.
QUALIFICATIONS
High school diploma or equivalent
Additional technical, manufacturing, or quality-related training preferred
EXPERIENCE
Minimum 1-3 years of manufacturing preferred
Previous experience in product inspection, stacking , packaging, or material handling preferred
Experience in composite decking, plastics, wood-plastic composites, or related manufacturing environments preferred
Prior leadership, training, or team lead experience preferred

title: Advanced Procedure Sales Manager
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion—have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you’ll find your purpose here.
*Please note: Candidates must live within or be willing to relocate to the Kansas City or St. Louis  Area to perform the duties of this role.
Primary Function of Position

Primary Function of Position
As a Senior Manager of Clinical Affairs, this role is responsible for contributing to clinical strategies and overseeing study execution for emerging technologies across various specialties.  Clinical trials in this portfolio may be both in the US and global and include first-human-use and pivotal clinical trials targeted for regulatory submission.  This role will oversee and manages clinical protocols and other key study documents in support of regulatory submissions; manage clinical publications and evidence dissemination strategy, oversee manage communications with clinical trial sites, CROs, KOLs and medical societies; grow, develop and manage team to interface and support all clinical requirements of the company with the applicable guidelines and regulations; foresee challenges and develops critical concepts and methodologies to overcome those.  As a functional manager, this role will also lead a team of clinical operations personnel, such as clinical study managers and clinical research associates and play a key role in their development.
As a key cross-functional constituent, this employee will work closely with functions across the organization – Regulatory Affairs, R&D, Program Management Office (PMO), Clinical Research Engineering (CRE), Clinical Research Managers, Global Access Value Economics (GAVE), Global Public Affairs (GPA), Regulatory Compliance, Training, Legal, and commercial functions to optimize clinical study strategies to meet business objectives.

Play a key role in the development of company’s strategy for clinical studies to meet business goals and objectives. Collaborate with internal stakeholders and KOLs to develop and review study concepts, protocol and study outlines and subsequently driving identified initiatives
Acting as a key strategic partner to Regulatory Affairs to support regulatory approval of new products and contribute to clinical sections of regulatory submissions
Responsible for managing resource and study budget to ensure clinical studies are conducted on schedule and within budget while ensuring high quality and compliance
Build strong and sustaining relationship with investigational sites and investigators for ongoing and future studies

title: Sr Supplier Engineer
description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Joining Intuitive Surgical means joining a team dedicated to using technology to benefit patients by improving surgical efficacy and decreasing surgical invasiveness, with patient safety as our highest priority.
Primary Function of Position:
The mission of Supplier Engineering is to ensure high quality and stable delivery of purchased production components from suppliers operating under robust quality systems . Each supplier engineer is responsible for ensuring suppliers meet ISI requirements for product quality, cost, and service.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Part Qualification
Support Value Engineering and Quality Improvement Part Qualification efforts
Lead Core Product Teams in defining appropriate Part Qualification requirements This includes defining testing and inspection requirements prior to system integration to maximize ISI factory efficiency
Support transfer of parts between suppliers

Manage the planning and implementation of supplier change management projects using the Supplier Change Request process (SCR) post Design V&V

Work cross-functionally to improve supplier engineering processes

Support Supplier Selection

Evaluate new supplies through informal assessments and formal assessment by supporting lead auditors in QMS evaluations

Manage supplier relationships to effectively partner with ISI suppliers

Plastic Injection Molding or other plastic forming processes
Die casting or Thixomolding
Proven ability to motivate suppliers and lead teams to solve difficult technical and process problems
Knowledge of pFMEA, process validation, inspection and test techniques

Ability to read and interpret detailed specifications and schematics and communicate technical information
Experience in a medical device company is a preferred
Experience with low-volume high-mix production environments is a preferred
Ability to travel to suppliers on an as needed basis – domestic and international

title: Analyst, Field Services
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Position Overview
The Operations Support Analyst will assist with a wide range of activities all directed toward the same goal:  maximizing the profitability of Invenergy’s Field Service divisions. Responsibilities include working closely with Asset management to track, make reclassifications to, and report on all aspects of the Field Service cost center by transforming data into actionable insights & business intelligence, and guiding data-driven decisions. Invenergy wants a team player willing to use their analytical, conceptual, and creative thinking skills to help with department growth and organization as well as look for ways to improve the group’s efficiency.
Responsibilities
Analyze data to assess how primary assumptions may affect pricing and/or returns.
Identify inconsistencies across models and provide feedback to management on how to ensure proper alignment of assumptions across job scopes.
Manage recurring reporting processes and identify actionable items
Provides support for day-to-day needs of the Operations Support team.
Develop other ad-hoc analyses as needed
Work alongside Field Service Management in the development and implementation of operational best practices
Act as a liaison between Asset Management, Accounting, and the Field Service Management team
Evaluate monthly charges to the Field Service cost center and reclassify them to their appropriate project cost center
Track the cost of and report on all Field Service work
Prepare and deliver customer invoicing for 3rd party Field Service work performed
Required Skills
2+ years professional related work experience
Ability to work effectively with all level of personnel and to work under minimal supervision
Excellent verbal and written communication skills

As an Imaging Lab Scientist , you will support the development and execution of digital and physical visualization solutions that enable faster, clearer, and more confident packaging and product decisions across the Kraft Heinz North America portfolio. The role also contributes creative problem-solving, concept translation, and innovative visualization approaches that help teams move from early ideas to actionable packaging decisions.

​​ ​Support execution of Imaging Lab requests by delivering digital and physical mock-ups, 3D models, and 3D-printed outputs that help teams evaluate packaging and product concepts, communicate design intent, and accelerate decision-making
​Create and produce package and label print outputs across film, carton, adhesive, and related materials to support development, visualization, and business needs

​
​Contribute innovative thinking and creative problem-solving to improve mock-up approaches, workflow execution, and the overall effectiveness of Imaging Lab support

​ Demonstrated creativity and innovation in solving visualization, mock-up, prototyping, or packaging-related challenges, with the ability to suggest new approaches that improve execution or project outcomes

You will be responsible for leading the security incident detection and response lifecycle and managing the ever-changing threat landscape through effective use of resources, threat intelligence, and training to mitigate the impact of global incidents. The list below is not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities.
What's on the menu?
Lead and manage the MSSP Security Operations Center, ensuring timely identification, analysis, containment, and remediation of global security events and incidents.
Create, implement, and maintain a strategic roadmap in collaboration with security leadership, including creating and maintaining KPIs and KRIs.
Conduct analysis of cyber incidents and remediate or recommend remediation as appropriate in accordance with established incident response processes (detection, triage, containment, incident analysis, remediation and reporting).
Conduct highly technical examinations, analysis and reporting of computer-based evidence related to security incidents (intrusion artifacts/IOCs) and investigations.
Develop and maintain Incident Response plans, playbooks, testing, and training for internal and external team members.
Develop and present recommendations for tuning security tools based on threat feeds, reputation data, events, or vulnerabilities and exploits of downstream systems.
Provides recommendations to resolve and/or reduce the impact of incidents and to prevent future incidents.
Collaborate with architecture, development, and engineering teams to identify the root cause of recurring incidents and create action plans for resolution.
Responsible for continuous improvement and overall program management for detection and Incident Response initiatives across people, process and technology, including training, communication, and relationship management with other business areas and vendor partners.
Identify and recommend opportunities for “clean slate” process improvement with regard to incident management.

I have 7+ years of relevant information security experience.
I have a demonstrated ability to translate technical incidents into business terms.
I have experience creating and presenting technical strategies and technical solution recommendations.
I have a thorough understanding of Security Operation Center, Incident Response, Threat Hunting, and enterprise digital forensics concepts (including proper investigation techniques, acquisition, chain of custody, preservation of evidence, validation, and sterilization).

title: Value Creation Business Partner (Spend Better)
description:
Job Description:
The Business Partner, Value Creation is a key member of the Integration Management Office (IMO) Value Creation team, reporting to the Value Creation Lead. The role serves as the primary value creation partner to assigned functions, regions, and integration workstreams, helping teams identify, quantify, track, and realize synergy commitments.
The Spend Better program is a critical pillar of the global Synergy program, focused on unlocking sustainable cost savings and productivity across the end-to-end value chain. Spend Better encompasses a broad range of value-creation opportunities, with an elevated emphasis on Directs (Direct Materials, Packaging, Recipe & Formulation, and Design-to-Value) alongside manufacturing productivity, network optimization, logistics efficiency, travel and overhead optimization, and other structural cost-reduction initiatives.
We are looking for a highly commercially oriented Finance Business Partner to partner the global Spend Better program and drive greater rigor, pace and intensity in delivering value. This role will operate at the intersection of Finance, Procurement, R&D, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Marketing and other functional teams. The successful candidate will work with senior stakeholders globally while partnering closely with Finance Business Partners across regions and functions.
The role requires someone who can identify opportunities, challenge assumptions, translate operational opportunities into financial value, and ensure that savings are both delivered and sustained.
What are we looking for?
10+ years of progressive Finance experience, ideally with significant experience in cost transformation, productivity, value creation or performance improvement.
Demonstrated experience across the Directs ecosystem— encompassing direct materials procurement finance, raw & packaging materials, R&D/formulation optimization, Design-to-Value (DtV), and Bill of Materials (BOM) cost architecture.
Substantial background in Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), Food & Beverage, or FMCG manufacturing environments where recipe, packaging, and factory conversion are central to cost structures.
Demonstrated experience translating operational productivity opportunities into validated, sustainable financial savings, with a strong understanding of manufacturing cost drivers and the ability to distinguish structural savings from volume, mix, inflation, FX and other financial effects.
Experience operating in large, complex, multinational organizations is strongly preferred.
Technical / Commercial Capability:
End-to-End Directs & Manufacturing Economics: Strong grasp of recipe costing, ingredient functionality trade-offs, packaging specifications, yield/scrap dynamics, and conversion economics.
Cost Engineering & DtV Acumen: Familiarity with teardowns, Design-to-Value principles, clean-sheet pricing, and supplier margin analysis.
Financial Modeling & Valuation: High proficiency in complex business cases, discounted cash flows, switchover investment paybacks, and synergy stage-gate tracking.
Financial Control & Accounting: Deep understanding of COGS, standard costing variance (purchase price variance, usage variance), P&L flow-through, and inventory valuation.

title: Data Center Technician Manager
description:
Overview
As a Microsoft Data Center Technician (DCT) Manager, you will lead a team of technicians, providing expert guidance on performing hardware deployments, diagnostics on equipment, and hardware decommissions. You will support technician performance, prioritizing technician tasks while monitoring Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Service Level Agreements (SLAs).  This opportunity will allow you to model leadership principles, provide training to technicians, and accelerate your career growth in the process.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I DCT Manager, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 data centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.

title: Principal Software Engineer
description:
Overview
We are looking for a Principal Software Engineer who lives and breathes Azure Cosmos DB and knows how it is implemented underneath. Your mission is to make throttling disappear from Microsoft's AI plugin registry with fast, surgical, high-ROI changes. Success is objective: throttling goes away, reliability goes up, and latency goes down, even as scale grows. You will see the results in days, not quarters.
We are the Agent Tools and Lifecycle team in Microsoft's Copilot, Agents and Platform (CAP) organization. We build the service behind the AI plugin registry. Admins use it in the Microsoft 365 admin center to govern the plugins (skills, connectors, and agents) that extend Microsoft Copilot, and users discover and use those plugins across products such as Copilot Chat, Cowork, Teams, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. The registry is a core part of Microsoft's AI architecture, alongside Work IQ, and Copilot experiences across Microsoft depend on it. If you use an AI solution from Microsoft, you likely are working with our service. Come join us at the center of AI transformation at Microsoft!
As a hands-on individual contributor, you will be the technical leader for the AI plugin registry's Azure Cosmos DB tier. Our catalog of plugins and agents, and the entitlements and policies that decide who can use them, live in Cosmos DB in data centers worldwide, including sovereign clouds. Traffic keeps growing as the registry expands to experiences such as Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot, and Microsoft Foundry. Experience working on the internals of Cosmos DB or a comparable database, such as MongoDB, Amazon DynamoDB, or Apache Cassandra, and an understanding of the hardware and network limits that make them throttle, are especially valuable. Our global reach means 24/7 on-call service.
This position is based in Redmond, Washington and requires the employee be in the office a minimum of 3 days per week.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Cut request unit (RU) consumption to make throttling go away, fast. Start with the queries that use the most RUs, where we see room for 50–90% reductions: turn cross-partition and fan-out queries into point reads from Cosmos DB or Azure Blob Storage, batched reads, or single-partition queries, and tune indexes.
Pick work by return on investment. Ship several targeted fixes in parallel, each within days, and measure each one in production. Take on a larger redesign only when the data shows smaller fixes cannot get there, and deliver it in steps that each pay off.
Fix hot partitions and size limits at the source: partition keys, document design, indexing policies, and API contracts that give high-traffic calls the keys they need for point reads. When data has to move, migrate it with zero downtime across all environments, including sovereign clouds.
Decide what belongs in Cosmos DB. Move large, binary, unbounded, or rarely queried content to Azure Blob Storage or other storage, weighing latency, availability, and data-residency needs.
Remove redundant and sequential database calls on our busiest paths with batching, request coalescing, and caching, and use retry budgets, load shedding, and graceful degradation so database pressure does not turn into failed requests.
Work with product management and the teams that call us to give each caller a throttling budget. Find callers that request the same unchanged data again and again, help them cache on their side, and lower the budgets of the heaviest callers over time.
Make success measurable: own the telemetry, dashboards, and alerts, RU use per API and per caller, partition skew, availability, and latency. Set targets, show the effect of every change, and spot limits before we hit them.
Raise the bar through AI: write AI skills that review designs and code for Cosmos DB mistakes, find high-RU queries, and show engineers how to fix them, so your expertise scales across the team. Use agentic tools to build and validate fixes faster, following Responsible AI practices. Mentor engineers and represent us with the Azure Cosmos DB product group.
Serve as a Designated Responsible Individual (DRI) in our 24/7 on-call rotation, lead data-tier incident response, and turn what we learn into lasting fixes.

OR equivalent experience.
4+ years of experience building or operating large-scale distributed databases, such as Azure Cosmos DB, MongoDB, Amazon DynamoDB, or Apache Cassandra, including partitioning, indexing, and query performance.

title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer, Data Center Equipment
description:
About the Team

OpenAI and its capital and technology partners are building a global network of data centers for demanding AI workloads. The Infrastructure Quality team sets and verifies quality, reliability, and performance requirements for equipment across that network.

We work with manufacturing partners, general contractors, engineers, and operations staff from supplier qualification through commissioning. Together, we verify that equipment arrives ready for installation, startup, and long-term service.

About the Role

As a Manufacturing Quality Engineer, you will oversee the quality of data center equipment at supplier factories. You will use production data, audits, and test results to identify systemic, recurring, or safety-related issues and work with suppliers to address them through Closed Loop Learning (CLL).

You will work with suppliers and internal teams to define inspections and factory tests for each type of equipment. You will coordinate issue resolution before shipment and manage deviations across multiple suppliers and project sites.

Key Responsibilities

Manufacturing Monitoring and Supplier Improvement

 - Manufacturing monitoring: Work with Manufacturing Operations to monitor production progress, quality controls, inspection results, and test readiness. Flag emerging risks and coordinate a response with suppliers.

 - Product and process audits: Audit products and processes during and after production against engineering requirements, critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics, approved procedures, and quality standards. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure.

 - Manufacturing coordination: Agree on production checkpoints and inspection and testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams. Escalate risks to equipment acceptance or delivery.

 - Manufacturing scorecards: Develop supplier and product scorecards with Manufacturing Operations. Review audit findings, test results, recurring defects, and open issues with suppliers to prioritize improvements.

 - Drive continuous improvement: Lead the CLL process with suppliers. Track root cause analyses and corrective and preventive actions in a shared register. Verify that each action addresses the underlying problem before closing it.

Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)

 - Standardize requirements and formats: Develop product-specific FAT requirements and standard test formats with equipment suppliers and OpenAI’s engineering, commissioning, quality, and Manufacturing Operations teams.

 - Define critical quality requirements: Document the CTQ characteristics each test must verify in an OpenAI-accepted format. Use CLL findings to revise FAT procedures so future tests check for known failure modes.

 - Ensure auditable supplier records: Require suppliers to retain test results and make them available for OpenAI audits.

 - Manage documentation and revision control: Review final FAT records and audit reports for each piece of equipment and maintain a controlled revision history.

 - Conduct periodic supplier audits: Check that suppliers follow approved test procedures and that their records accurately reflect the tests performed.

Factory Witness Testing (FWT)

 - Align checklists and stakeholders: Develop standard FWT checklists with OpenAI subject matter experts, installing contractors, and the construction management team. Agree on requirements before testing begins.

 - Manage documentation and reporting: Collect and review final witness test reports and supporting records from participants.

 - Before shipment, confirm that each witness-test issue is resolved or covered by a documented deviation. Log systemic, recurring, or safety-related findings in the CLL tracker and verify the effectiveness of corrective actions with the supplier.

Deviation Management

 - Assess short shipments and missing or failed tests in partnership with Manufacturing Operations.

 - Coordinate supplier support to resolve issues at the project site.

 - Document each deviation and track the agreed actions through closure.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, or industrial engineering.

 - At least 10 years of data center industry experience spanning quality engineering and project management.

 - Experience coordinating FAT and FWT with suppliers and resolving equipment quality issues.

 - Ability to develop test checklists, define CTQs, review test results, and maintain auditable quality records.

 - Experience monitoring supplier production, auditing products and processes during and after production, and using scorecards to improve supplier and product quality. Experience managing controlled documents and deviations.

 - Ability to coordinate supplier schedules and plan inspections and tests across multiple pieces of equipment.

 - Ability to communicate quality requirements and coordinate decisions across suppliers, engineering, commissioning, sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, quality, and construction teams.

 - Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40–60% of the time to supplier manufacturing facilities and data center project sites.

Preferred Skills

 - Technical knowledge of data center infrastructure, including mechanical, electrical, and controls systems.

 - Experience in supplier performance management for mission-critical facilities.

 - ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Quality Manager, or Quality Auditor.

 - PMP or equivalent project management certification.

 - Experience in industrial or high-volume manufacturing environments.
