Join Our Team as a Mechanical Quality Technologist!
The Mechanical Quality Technologist is responsible for inspecting and testing mechanical assemblies, subassemblies, and parts within a manufacturing environment. This role ensures that mechanical components meet quality standards by conducting thorough inspections and tests according to established procedures. The role involves interpreting mechanical drawings, specifications, and test results, and documenting inspection results. The position requires strong attention to detail, a solid understanding of quality inspection methods, and the ability to operate mechanical testing equipment.
Key Responsibilities:
Perform inspections of mechanical subassemblies, final assemblies, and other mechanical fixtures to ensure compliance with product specifications and quality standards.
Verify that mechanical components are assembled correctly and that tolerances meet established criteria.
Interpret mechanical drawings, bills of materials (BOMs), and technical documentation to ensure compliance with design and production standards.
Record and document inspection results, identifying non-conforming products and initiating corrective action as required.
Utilize, maintain, and calibrate mechanical testing equipment, ensuring it is in proper working condition.
Collaborate with production teams to address quality issues and suggest improvements to processes.
Assist in developing and improving testing procedures and protocols based on findings and feedback.
Understand and follow ISO 9001 standards and ensure compliance in daily work.
Maintain detailed inspection logs and reports for review by supervisors.
Assist in maintaining the safety of the work area by following relevant safety guidelines for handling mechanical components and equipment.
Continuously develop skills related to mechanical testing and inspection techniques, with a focus on pursuing relevant certifications (e.g., ASQ, ASME).
Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
Work with departmental mentors to gain and apply feedback in pursuit of improved work quality.
Other responsibilities as assigned.
What you’ll need to succeed:
Required
High school diploma.
3+ years of hands-on manufacturing experience, such as assembly.
Sound understanding of mechanical systems. Able to complete troubleshooting tasks to identify issues within these systems.
Ability to understand part drawings, Bills of Material, Sales Orders, & Technical Documents.
Good understanding of ISO 9001.
Willingness to work in a manufacturing environment on a product floor and open to learning new concepts of mechanical/product testing.
Proficient in performing precise and delicate tasks using hands and fingers. Able to manipulate small objects, operate tools, and handle intricate equipment effectively.
Sound attention to detail, with the ability to follow detailed instructions and identify correct vs. incorrect product functions.
Rounded communication skills (written and verbal) with the ability to articulate information efficiently and effectively to team members in a variety of production support departments.
Good computer skills with the ability to review and respond to requests and use Microsoft/ERP applications.
Ability to use hand tools and precision measuring equipment.
Good shop math skills with the ability to calculate measurements.
Good interpersonal and organizational skills with the ability to understand and complete requests given by team members inside and outside of the department.
Ability and willingness to follow Health, Safety & Environment procedures accurately, reporting concerns promptly to the safety action team.
Preferred
Associate degree in a trade or related mechanical/electrical field.
ASQ Certification
Experience working in an inspection role in a manufacturing organization.
Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement manufacturing principles.

Sitting: Continuously required to stand and perform tasks.
Walking: Frequently required to walk moderate distances across the S&C campus.
Manual Dexterity: Frequently required to use hand-eye coordination to control both hands and arms for a full range of motion to operate equipment/machinery/power tools/office productivity equipment.

Make evals a first-class discipline. Design evaluation frameworks for agent and LLM behavior, including golden datasets, LLM-as-judge, human review loops, and regression suites, and run them in development and production. Use transcript analysis and eval results to find failures, guide what to fix first, and show quality improving over time.
Lead with AI day to day. Use agents, coding assistants, and agent harnesses in your own daily work, and build the shared tooling, patterns, and harnesses that make the whole team faster.

Automatically included

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant work experience.
Hands-on experience building and shipping LLM applications and agentic workflows to production, including tool use, retrieval, context engineering, and production reliability.
Production full-stack and cloud engineering experience (for example Python or TypeScript, AWS, and Databricks), including owning systems that other teams depend on.

Daily, fluent use of AI agents and coding assistants in your own work, and a point of view on how they change the way teams build.
A track record of shipping internal or customer-facing AI/ML products with measurable business impact.
Experience with predictive modeling, experimentation, analytics, and data engineering foundations.
Strong product judgment and the ability to turn ambiguous business problems into simple, valuable solutions.

Experience with agent SDKs and harnesses (such as Claude Code / Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, or similar) and LLM observability tooling, eval tooling such as Braintrust or MLflow, and model APIs from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google.
Experience operating AI products at scale, including cost management, monitoring, and governance.
A visible habit of learning in public, such as writing, talks, open-source work, or internal “what’s new in AI” sessions.

Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. Samsara builds an extensive set of products, including battery-powered, wireless sensors, Linux-based IoT gateways, and Internet-connected dashcams. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.
As a Firmware Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.
We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.
Click here to learn more about Samsara's cultural philosophy.
In this role, you will:
Shape the hardware, not just the code that runs on it. Sit in reviews with our electrical engineers and help choose the right SoC, amount of flash/RAM, and combination of sensors, then prove those choices out on prototypes that reach real customers in months, not years.
Be the first person to make a new board do anything at all. Bring up new platforms and prototypes from virgin silicon: configure I/O, get SPI, I2C, UART, BLE talking, debug system init, validate the design, and turn unproven hardware into a product.
Build the layers everything else depends on. Peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders, device firmware updates, as well as the core management layers like power and connectivity, that determine whether a device in the field quietly recovers on its own or becomes an RMA.
Chase every microamp. Design protocols and hardware management for battery-powered sensors and gateways where the gap between good firmware and great firmware is measured in years of device life.
Work with the people who ship the whole product. Partner with product, full-stack, mobile and quality engineers so the data your firmware produces arrives intact and useful as it lands in the hands of dispatchers, fleet managers, and technicians who depend on it every shift.
Raise the bar for the engineers around you. Your designs, reviews, and instincts help raise the ceiling for the whole team. You will help shape how Samsara works, keep a high bar, be intellectually honest, work with urgency and deliver iteratively, as we scale globally and across new offices.
What you bring
2+ years building firmware for resource-constrained systems , on products that shipped to real customers and then had to survive in the field.
Fluency in C. You know what the compiler is doing, and you can read a linker map, a stack trace, or a corrupted heap without guessing.
Solid bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.
You have helped bring up new boards. First power-on of unproven hardware, at the bench with the electrical engineer who drew it up, working out whether the bug is in your code, a library, the schematic, or the part itself.
Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.
Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.
Cross-team scope. You have contributed to work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have worked effectively across teams to build consensus.
Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you factor that into your design decisions.
You write things down. Design docs, review comments and post-mortems that other engineers can actually act on.
You ship fast without shipping poorly. Comfortable iterating on customer feedback at speed, backed by automated testing and code you would be content to inherit.
You use AI smartly. It’s part of your every day work flow and multiplies your output without watering things down.
What will set you apart
BLE at depth - You understand what’s going on down the PHY and can build orchestration for the system to use in a performant and power efficient way.
Cellular IoT - LTE-M or NB-IoT modem integration, power state management, and the certification gauntlet (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approval).
Securing embedded systems end to end - secure boot, firmware signing, cryptography, and key management that survives contact with manufacturing.
OTA and device firmware update at fleet scale - A/B partitions, rollback, and the discipline of never bricking a device you cannot physically reach.
Embedded Linux on the gateway side - Yocto or Buildroot, kernel drivers, device trees.
CAN and J1939 work on commercial vehicles , including reverse-engineering data bus parameters across makes and models.
Python and Bash for tooling , and hardware-in-the-loop test automation.
You’ve been on the factory floor - You have an understanding of the processes behind the mass production and quality assurance of electronics. You have a track record of fixing production show stoppers.

title: Internal Purchasing Specialist
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.

About the role

You're the front door for everything Standard Bots buys to build, test, and demo physical robots: prototype parts, test fixtures, shop tools, pilot and trade-show builds. Engineers and customer-facing teams count on you to get what they need fast, and you'll keep the controls tight while you do it. And you won't do it by hand forever: you'll build AI-assisted workflows so routine requests move with almost no manual touch.

📍 Location

This is a full-time, remote role open to candidates in the US. You'll sit on the Finance team, report to the Accounting Manager, and work closely with teams across the company.

What you'll do

- Run the internal purchasing queue end to end: intake, clarify specs, source, buy, track delivery, and close out.

- Respond to every request within one business day and turn standard purchases around the same day.

- Triage urgent R&D and customer POC needs so engineering work never sits blocked waiting on a purchase.

- Keep requesters posted on status, ETAs, and substitutions, so nobody has to chase you.

- Find the right vendor on price, lead time, and quality, and get quotes on larger purchases.

- Set up and maintain vendors in Ramp, including W-9s, payment terms, and vendor ownership.

- Build a preferred-vendor list and negotiate pricing or accounts with high-volume suppliers.

- Issue POs, confirm receipt, and act as vendor owner and first invoice reviewer. The Accounting Manager is the second approver.

- Enforce the purchasing policy and approval thresholds, and route exceptions to the right budget owner.

- Tag every purchase with the correct GL account, department, and project, so R&D, POC, and capex costs are clean at month-end.

- Flag fixed-asset purchases to the Accounting Manager with the details needed for capitalization and asset tagging.

- Keep records audit-ready, with approvals, quotes, receipts, and invoices tied to each PO.

- Roll out the move from open Ramp card spend to centralized purchasing: communicate the change, train teams, and manage the transition.

- Report monthly on spend by department, category, and vendor, plus cycle time and open requests.

- Spot recurring purchases and convert them into standing orders, catalogs, or blanket POs.

What you'll bring

- 3+ years in purchasing, procurement, or purchasing-focused operations, ideally at a hardware, robotics, or manufacturing company.

- Hands-on experience with a spend management platform (Ramp, Brex, Coupa, or similar) and PO-based purchasing.

- Working knowledge of basic accounting concepts: GL coding, capex vs. opex, accruals, and three-way match.

- Ai Automation - this role scales through automation, not headcount. You’ll build AI agents to run intake, vendor comparisons, POs, invoice matching, and status updates, document every workflow so others can run it, and keep pushing up the share of requests that close with no manual touch.

- A service mindset: you're fast, responsive, and comfortable juggling many small requests at once.

- Strong judgment on when to follow policy and when to escalate.

Nice to have

- Experience standing up a purchasing function or rolling out a new spend policy.

- Exposure to audit-ready controls and fixed-asset tracking.

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $70,000 - $85,000 depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: Staff Systems Engineer, Simulation Systems Verification and Validation Lead

We are seeking a Simulation Systems Verification and Validation (Sim VnV) Lead to own that work across the full autonomy stack. You will define how to validate simulation at the sensor, perception, planning, and full-pipeline levels, lead the cross-functional program that executes the sim VnV program, and turn the results into clear evidence about when and where simulated miles can support safety clearance decisions. You will work closely with simulation, perception, planning, hardware, safety, data science, and systems engineering teams. This is a highly visible, technical leadership role on the critical path to safely scaling our service. The ideal candidate demonstrates systems thinking, can lead a complex program across teams, and knows how to validate a model of a closed-loop system that has an AI controller inside it. In this role, you will:

  • Own the end-to-end simulation V&V strategy across different levels of integration ranging from sensors-only through the full system behavior for the purpose of constructing a safety case for fully autonomous driving on public roads.

  • Define the data sets, metrics, and comparison methods.

  • Lead a recurring cross-functional sim validation program with simulation, perception, planning, systems engineering, safety, and data infrastructure teams. Set milestones and cadence, track risks and dependencies, and drive decisions to closure.

  • Partner with statisticians and data scientists on estimators that combine simulated and real-world results into safety performance measures.

  • Write the methodology documents and validation reports, and present results, risks, and recommendations to engineering and executive leadership.

  • Mentor engineers across teams in V&V practice and systems thinking.

    • Qualifications

  • M.S. or higher in Systems, Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, or Robotics Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, or a related field.

  • 8+ years of experience in verification and validation of safety-critical systems that contain software or autonomy (for example autonomous vehicles, ADAS, aerospace guidance and flight software, or robotics).

  • A record of leading technical programs across several teams, from an ambiguous problem statement to a delivered result.

  • Working-level experience validating a simulation or model against real-world data so that its results could support a decision, preferably for a closed-loop system with software or a learned controller in the loop.

  • Strong systems thinking: you can break a system into integration levels, define the interfaces and the evidence needed at each level, and connect component-level results to system-level claims.

  • Experience deriving or implementing estimators that fuse simulated and real data, for example control variates, prediction-powered inference, Bayesian hierarchical models or power priors, importance sampling, or rare-event estimation. Similar experience with modeling uncertainties and failure rates is also acceptable.

    • Bonus Qualifications

  • Experience with sensor simulation (camera, lidar, radar), neural rendering or generative scene synthesis, or perception evaluation metrics.

  • Experience evaluating motion planning or behavior in closed-loop simulation at scale.

  • Familiarity with model credibility and safety standards, such as NASA-STD-7009, ASME V&V 10/20/40, ISO 21448 (SOTIF), UL 4600, ISO 26262, or ISO 34502.

  • Hands-on Python and SQL.

  • Ph.D. in a relevant field.

title: Joint Head of Pricing, Promotions & Analytics
location: United States of America - Kentucky - Louisville
description:
Job Family Group:
Marketing Group
Job Description:
The Head of Pricing & Data Analytics – Merchandising is responsible for building and leading the pricing and analytics capabilities that support the Merchandising organization across BP and TA brands . This role will use data, analytics, competitive intelligence, customer insights, and advanced pricing technology to improve sales, margin, inventory productivity, and the overall customer value proposition.
The position will play a key leadership role in helping develop, implement, and expand the use of BP's enterprise pricing tool/system across its brands . This includes partnering with Merchandising, Pricing, Operations, Loyalty, and other key stakeholders to determine how the platform can best support the business and ensuring its capabilities translate into practical, actionable pricing recommendations.
This leader will manage a team of data scientists and analytics professionals responsible for turning complex data into clear, actionable recommendations. The team will provide insights and recommendations across all merchandise categories, including base pricing, promotional pricing, markdowns, competitive positioning, assortment, inventory, and other sales and margin opportunities .
The role will also own and manage the Store Archetype Strategy , ensuring merchandising decisions reflect the different customers, missions, sales opportunities, and operating environments across the store network.
Additionally, this leader will ensure that pricing, promotional, customer, and store archetype insights effectively support EarnifyPro and other loyalty programs as part of the overall Merchandising strategy. The role will partner with Loyalty and other key stakeholders to help develop more relevant offers, increase customer engagement, and ensure loyalty strategies complement the broader pricing and promotional strategy.
The overarching objective is to use data, analytics, pricing technology, and customer insights to help put the right products, in the right stores, at the right price, in the right quantities, with the right offers for the right customers.
Key Responsibilities
Enterprise Pricing Strategy & Pricing System
Help develop, implement, and continuously improve the use of the enterprise pricing tool/system across BP and TA brands .
Work across the broader BP organization to identify opportunities to leverage the pricing platform's advanced analytics and AI capabilities.
Partner with Category Management and Merchandising leadership to establish an effective and consistent pricing framework while recognizing differences in customers, markets, brands, and store formats.
Help translate the capabilities of the pricing system into practical business processes and actionable recommendations for Category Managers and leadership.
Drive adoption and effective utilization of the pricing system within Merchandising.
Develop and provide data-driven recommendations for: Base and everyday pricing
Promotional pricing
Markdown and clearance strategies
Competitive price positioning
Price zones and geographic pricing
Price elasticity and customer response
Margin and sales optimization
Establish processes for regularly reviewing pricing performance and identifying opportunities for improvement.
Ensure pricing recommendations balance customer value, competitive position, sales growth, margin, and long-term category health .
Develop clear reporting that allows leadership and Category Managers to understand the expected and actual impact of pricing decisions.
Measure results and continuously refine pricing strategies based on performance.
Data Science & Advanced Analytics
Lead, develop, and mentor a team of data scientists and analytics professionals supporting Merchandising.
Establish priorities for the team based on the most significant sales, margin, inventory, pricing, and customer opportunities.
Translate large and complex data sets into practical recommendations that Category Managers and business leaders can act upon .
Develop analytics around customer behavior, product performance, pricing, promotions, loyalty, inventory, assortment, and store segmentation.
Identify trends and opportunities that may not be visible through traditional merchandising reporting.
Leverage advanced analytics and AI capabilities to improve the quality, speed, and predictive nature of merchandising decisions.
Build analytical capabilities that move the organization beyond simply reporting what happened toward understanding why it happened, what is likely to happen next, and what actions should be taken .
Create scorecards and measurement tools that clearly demonstrate the financial and operational impact of merchandising decisions.
Store Archetype Strategy
Own and continuously develop the Store Archetype Strategy for Merchandising.
Use customer, sales, demographic, geographic, competitive, operational, loyalty, and store-level data to define meaningful store groups and customer missions.
Partner with Category Management and Space Planning to ensure assortments, space allocation, pricing, promotions, and inventory strategies reflect the needs of each archetype.
Help determine which products should be carried by store type and where assortment should expand, contract, or vary.
Use archetype analytics to help determine appropriate inventory levels and quantities by store.
Incorporate customer and loyalty behavior into archetype development to better understand who is shopping each type of location and what drives their purchasing decisions.
Continuously evaluate store performance and refine archetypes as customer behavior and business conditions change.
Ensure the archetype strategy becomes an actionable merchandising tool rather than simply a store classification exercise .
Loyalty & EarnifyPro Integration
Partner with the EarnifyPro and broader loyalty teams to ensure merchandising pricing, promotional, customer, and archetype insights support the overall loyalty strategy.
Use customer and transaction data to identify opportunities for targeted and personalized offers based on customer behavior, store archetype, geography, category, and shopping mission.
Help determine when the business should use base price, broad-based promotions, loyalty-specific offers, or targeted customer offers to produce the best overall result.
Evaluate loyalty offers based on incremental sales, margin, trips, basket size, customer engagement, and return on investment.
Ensure loyalty promotions work in coordination with the overall Merchandising promotional calendar rather than operating as a separate strategy.
Use the enterprise pricing system and other analytical capabilities, where appropriate, to identify pricing and promotional opportunities that can be activated through EarnifyPro or other loyalty platforms.
Provide Merchandising leadership and Category Managers with insights into how loyalty customers respond differently to products, pricing, promotions, and categories.
Partner with Loyalty leadership to identify opportunities to increase frequency, retention, cross-category purchasing, and overall customer value .
Help ensure the organization understands the interaction between pricing, promotions, loyalty, and customer behavior rather than evaluating each independently.
Merchandising Decision Support
Serve as a strategic analytics partner to Category Managers and Merchandising leadership.
Provide Category Managers with fact-based recommendations while ensuring their category expertise, vendor knowledge, and market understanding remain an important part of the decision-making process.
Identify opportunities to improve sales, margin, turns, inventory productivity, and customer value.
Support assortment rationalization and SKU productivity analysis.
Evaluate promotional effectiveness and recommend changes based on incremental sales, margin, customer response, and overall return.
Develop markdown recommendations designed to efficiently exit discontinued, aged, seasonal, and underperforming inventory.
Identify opportunities where changes in assortment, pricing, promotion, loyalty offers, or inventory levels could improve category performance.
Help leadership prioritize opportunities based on potential financial impact and ease of execution.
Leadership Expectations
Build a highly capable, commercially focused pricing and analytics organization .
Develop team members who understand both data science and the practical realities of retail merchandising .
Create a culture where analytics leads to action rather than simply producing reports.
Communicate complex analytical findings in clear business terms that can be understood and acted upon at all levels of the organization.
Work collaboratively across BP, TA, Merchandising, Operations, Loyalty, and other key functions , while being willing to challenge existing practices when the data supports a different approach.
Help create consistency and share learnings across BP brands while recognizing that different brands, customers, and store formats may require different strategies.
Ensure analytical recommendations consider the impact on the customer and the ability of stores to execute.
Maintain a strong focus on practical, scalable solutions that produce measurable business results .
Qualifications & Experience
Significant leadership experience in retail pricing, merchandising analytics, data science, category analytics, or a related discipline .
Demonstrated experience building or leading high-performing analytics or data science teams.
Strong understanding of retail pricing concepts, including base pricing, promotional pricing, markdown optimization, competitive pricing, and price elasticity.
Experience implementing, developing, or optimizing enterprise retail pricing and analytics platforms strongly preferred.
Experience using advanced analytics, AI, or predictive modeling to support retail pricing and merchandising decisions.
Experience with store segmentation, clustering, archetypes, assortment analytics, or localized merchandising strongly preferred.
Understanding of retail loyalty programs, customer segmentation, personalization, and targeted promotional strategies.
Strong financial and commercial understanding with the ability to connect analytical recommendations to sales, margin, inventory, customer behavior, and profitability.
Proven ability to turn complex analytical findings into practical business recommendations.
Strong communication and influencing skills with the ability to work effectively across multiple brands and with senior leadership, Category Managers, Operations, Loyalty, and other cross-functional partners.
Measures of Success
Success in this role will ultimately be measured by the ability to use pricing, analytics, customer insights, and store archetypes to produce measurable business results, including:
Successful implementation, adoption, and continued development of the enterprise pricing tool/system across BP and TA brands
Improved sales and gross margin performance
More effective base and promotional pricing
Improved promotional ROI
Faster and more effective markdown execution
Improved inventory productivity and turns
Better localized assortments and inventory levels
Improved in-stock performance
Reduced unproductive and aged inventory
Increased adoption of data-driven decision making across Merchandising
Effective execution and continued development of the Store Archetype Strategy
Increased effectiveness and ROI of merchandising-related loyalty offers
Growth in loyalty-driven trips, transactions, basket size, and incremental sales
Improved coordination between base pricing, promotions, markdowns, and loyalty offers
Increased use of customer and loyalty insights in merchandising decisions
Increased sharing of pricing insights, capabilities, and best practices across BP brands

We’re committed to supporting leaders who want to make an impact. You’ll have the chance to shape and influence outcomes across businesses. You’ll be part of an inclusive environment where diverse perspectives are valued, and where your contribution to performance and integration matters.

Our total rewards package includes competitive pay, bonuses, share options, and a range of flexible benefits designed to meet your needs. We recognise that people have multifaceted lives, and we strive to offer a career experience that reflects that.

location: United States of America - Kansas - Shawnee
description:
Job Family Group:
Operations Group
Job Description:
About Archaea
bp is committed to investing in lower carbon energy so we can meet our ambition to reach net zero by 2050. And while we’re still mostly in oil and gas today, bioenergy is one of our five transition growth engines and a key focus to help us support the global energy transition.
Archaea Energy, a bp company, is a leader in landfill gas to energy and the largest renewable natural gas (RNG) producer in the US. With big ambitions, we specialize in the development, construction and operation of RNG, landfill-gas-to-electric and dairy digester facilities. The team operates around 50 sites in 32 states with a robust development pipeline.
About the role
The Operations Technician is responsible for the overall safe operation, maintenance, and performance of a landfill gas to Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) processing facility.  This position requires 25%-50% travel per month (First 12 months in the position will require 50% travel per month when hired for a new plant. Travel requirement will reduce to 25% per month when working at an existing plant or in year 2 and beyond for a new plant).
Key accountabilities
Manage the safe operation of the plant during assigned shift in the most efficient and productive method to maintain compliance with Standard Operating Procedures (SOP’s) and prescribed safety and environmental standards.
Make periodic inspections of plant equipment to determine proper and normal operating conditions. Check and record operational data such as fluid levels, temperatures and pressures, compare to trends and have the ability to make corrections as needed.
Review daily operating reports and other records to ensure specified operating characteristics in control of the plant equipment.
Perform preventive maintenance and troubleshooting on plant instrumentation and equipment.
Detect and correct faulty and malfunctioning mechanical and electrical components, devices and equipment.
Operate advanced instrumentation and process control systems.
Diagnose equipment malfunctions during emergencies and direct activities to restore normal operation or to shut down malfunctioning unit.
Test electrical systems and continuity of circuits in electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures using testing devices such as ohmmeters and voltmeters.
Troubleshoot and repair electrical system wiring from control wiring up to 480 volts. Install, remove and modify equipment.
Notify Lead Operation Technician and Regional Manager of shutdown or major changes in power output of unit.
Maintain all plant equipment and structures in accordance with manufactures and Aria Energy guidelines.
Maintain a clean work space including the plant building, control room, rest room, break room and grounds.
Write routine reports and correspondence.
Maintain daily operation logs for shift in accordance with prescribed standards.
Assist in planning maintenance and outage activities.
Assist in defining, ordering and procuring all required parts.
Responds in a timely manner to callouts and work overtime as required
Perform analytical tests as needed (i.e. PH, Conductivity, methane, H2S, moisture).
Implement all safety procedures to included lockout tag out procedures.
Perform all aspects of Hazardous waste handling and management in accordance with training. Duties may range from filling of waste containers, proper labeling, movement of containers, completing appropriate paperwork, and signing of Hazardous waste shipping manifest or receiving hazardous products.
This position requires 25%-50% travel per month (First 12 months in the position will require 50% travel per month when hired for a new plant. Travel requirement will reduce to 25% per month when working at an existing plant or in year 2 and beyond for a new plant).
Essential education
Requires a High School Diploma or equivalent.
Essential experience
Intermediate Electrical, Chemical and Mechanical experience.
Previous landfill gas operation experience a plus, minimum of 1-3 years in landfill gas processing, chemical plant operations, industrial gas operations, or power plant operations or equivalent.
3+ years’ experience in landfill gas processing, or power plant operations
Any technical certification or training is a plus.
Desirable criteria
Understanding of process control systems as applied to landfill gas collection and processing.
Technical / Troubleshooting skills with ability to read and understand complex technical manuals and schematics.
Understanding a variety of sensors and transducer systems, calibrate, and troubleshoot different types of pressure, level, flow and temperature sensors, understand the complete plant process and how it’s affected by the control system, including troubleshooting mechanical systems as required.
Knowledge of basic math, gas chemistry, piping and instrumentation drawings.
Ability to read blueprints and follow established procedures with minimal amount of general supervision (i.e., work independently).
Ability to recognize colors, able to distinguish between the red and green status indicators on PLC and wire colors.
Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.
Ability to write routine reports and correspondence.
Ability to speak effectively to employees of the organization.
Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables.
Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.
Proficient using computers (experience using MS Word, Excel and email systems) and monitoring equipment to measure, record and make adjustments within operating parameters, perform fault finding and repair as well as required scheduled maintenance.

Hands-on mechanical and process equipment.
Previous landfill and or gas processing experience

title: Planner/Scheduler
location: United States of America - Colorado - Denver
description:
Job Family Group:
Operations Group
Job Description:
bpx energy, a major oil and gas producer in the United States, leverages its expertise in unconventional gas, including shale, to deliver hydrocarbon production and technical knowledge worldwide. With operations in Texas and Louisiana, our US onshore business has become both a premier oil and gas producer and a leader in reducing methane emissions.
As part of BP, a global industry leader, we foster a high-energy, high-intensity environment built on accountability, collegiality, innovation, and empowerment. At bpx, we support our people to learn and grow in a diverse and challenging environment where collaboration, continuous improvement, and inclusion are valued.
Discover your place with us and help our business meet the challenges of reimagining and reinventing the future of energy.
Role Synopsis
The Planner / Scheduler plans and schedules maintenance, instrumentation and electrical (I&E), brownfield construction, and greenfield construction work across Permian production operations. The role helps develop field-ready work packages, integrates resource and material requirements, manages the work-order backlog, and builds realistic weekly and monthly schedules that support safe, efficient execution.
Reporting to the Construction & Maintenance Manager, this position serves as the central coordination point among Operations, Maintenance, I&E, Construction, Reliability, Engineering, Supply Chain, warehouse personnel, contractor resources, and our Midstream partners. The Planner / Scheduler identifies constraints and conflicts before work reaches the field, aligns work with operating and shutdown windows, and helps minimize production impacts and avoidable schedule disruption.
Success requires proficiency in SAP as the work management system, disciplined use of the work-management process and supporting systems, strong field engagement, practical knowledge of maintenance and construction execution, and the ability to turn competing priorities into a clear, executable plan. The role owns planning quality, schedule readiness, backlog visibility, schedule-performance reporting, and continuous improvement through feedback from execution teams.
Key Accountabilities
Work planning and job readiness
Develop detailed work packages that define scope, work steps, labor, materials, tools, equipment, permits, isolations, safety requirements, access needs, and completion criteria.
Perform field walkdowns with Operations and execution teams to validate scope, identify constraints, and confirm site readiness before work is committed to the schedule.
Estimate job durations and resource requirements using historical performance, job complexity, and crew capability.
Confirm materials, rentals, contractor support, and long-lead items are identified, ordered, tracked, staged, and available before mobilization.
Integrated scheduling and coordination
Build and maintain integrated weekly and monthly schedules for Maintenance, I&E, construction, shutdown, turnaround, and commissioning activities.
Facilitate schedule-development and readiness meetings with team leads and partner functions; document priorities, owners, constraints, decisions, and schedule changes.
Balance workload across internal crews and contractors while identifying conflicts, capacity gaps, and competing resource demands early.
Coordinate work with Operations to align access, isolations, production impacts, outage windows, and return-to-service requirements.
Protect committed construction and maintenance milestones by communicating risks early and presenting practical recovery or resource options.
Backlog and work-management governance
Manage the work-order backlog through prioritization, aging, status review, scope validation, and escalation of work requiring leadership attention.
Maintain accurate work-order, equipment, PM, schedule, and completion data in the SAP and associated planning tools.
Coordinate timely closeout of completed work, including actual labor hours, materials used, execution feedback, and required documentation.
Promote adherence to the work-management process and continuously improve planning quality through feedback loops with field crews and team leads.
Performance, cost, and continuous improvement
Track and report schedule compliance, planning accuracy, planned-versus-unplanned work, backlog health, material readiness, carryover, break-in work, and work-order closeout performance.
Analyze maintenance and construction data to identify recurring constraints, productivity losses, cost drivers, and opportunities to improve PM strategies and execution efficiency.
Support cost transparency by aligning planned labor, contractor, equipment, and material requirements with approved work scopes and budgets.
Identify opportunities to combine work within common outage windows to reduce repeat mobilization, production deferral, and operational disruption.
Essential Experience and Education
High school diploma or equivalent.
Demonstrated experience planning or scheduling maintenance, construction, turnaround, or operations work in oil and gas, industrial, manufacturing, utilities, or a comparable asset-intensive environment.
Working knowledge of work-order planning, backlog management, preventive and corrective maintenance, job readiness, permitting, isolation, and contractor coordination.
Proficiency using SAP as a work management system to create and maintain work orders, support planning and scheduling, manage backlog visibility, and report on executable work plans.
Ability to perform field walkdowns and work effectively in an operating production environment.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to facilitate cross-functional planning meetings and communicate schedule risks, trade-offs, and decisions.
Desirable Criteria
Experience supporting upstream oil and gas production, wellsite facilities, gathering systems, or related Permian Basin operations.
Experience coordinating multi-discipline Maintenance, I&E, Construction, Reliability, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, warehouse, and contractor work.
Experience with shutdown, turnaround, tie-in, commissioning, and new-well facility scheduling.
Experience developing work packages, managing long-lead materials, and using schedule and backlog metrics to improve crew productivity.
Post-secondary technical training, trade certification, associate degree, or bachelor's degree in maintenance, construction management, engineering technology, operations, supply chain, or a related field.
Safety-focused and field-oriented, with disciplined attention to job readiness and control-of-work requirements.
Organized and detail-driven, with the ability to manage multiple work streams and changing priorities without losing accountability.
Collaborative and influential across functions, with the confidence to challenge incomplete scopes and unrealistic schedules constructively.
Analytical and improvement-minded, using data and execution feedback to strengthen planning quality and schedule performance.
Pragmatic and accountable, with a strong bias toward clear ownership, timely decisions, and executable plans.
